question: Should maintainers accept a narrow terminal-status repair for declined Codex-native approvals while keeping https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99645 open, or require the full native-denial recovery contract before merge?
rationale: The canonical issue asks for continuation, sibling-result preservation, and user-visible failure delivery; this PR can be a useful partial fix only if maintainers accept that narrower scope.

options.title: Narrow Repair, Keep Issue Open
options.body: Require the no-stop-reason classifier fix and real behavior proof, then land this as a partial terminal-status invariant while leaving the broader contract issue open.

options.title: Hold For Full Contract
options.body: Keep this PR unmerged until continuation, sibling-result preservation, and outbound terminal-failure delivery are implemented together.

options.title: Close As Too Narrow
options.body: Ask for a replacement PR if maintainers do not want partial native-denial fixes that leave the central contract unresolved.

recommendation.title: Narrow Repair, Keep Issue Open
recommendation.body: Require the no-stop-reason classifier fix and real behavior proof, then land this as a partial terminal-status invariant while leaving the broader contract issue open.
